narr: On June 3 and 4, a cold front and a dryline served as focal points for thunderstorm development across North and Central Texas. These storms were associated with several instances of severe weather and flooding. Unfortunately Unfortunately one person died due to flooding in Dallas County, and a lightning strike killed one person and severely injured another person in Grayson County.
ev: A report from mPING indicated street/road flooding; street/road closed; and vehicles stranded.

Emergency management reported that several roads were flooded and closed across Rowlett, including Princeton Rd at Coventry Dr, Rowlett Rd at Miller Rd with two stranded vehicles, Hwy 66 at Sprouts Dr with three stranded vehicles, and Rowlett Rd at Locust St with five vehicles stranded. A member of the public also reported that five homes were flooded with about one foot deep of water on Scott Drive.
Broadcast media reported that a section of I-35 was flooded and impassable in Lewisville.

Emergency management reported that several roads sustained flood damage to bridges and culverts, or had areas of the roadway washed away, including County Roads 3715, 1500, 1507, 3822, 3918, 1113 near the city of Athens, and FM 316 near the city of Athens.
Several roads were reported flooded and closed across Garland including Campbell Road, Castle Drive and Naaman School Road.

Law enforcement, trained spotters and the public reported several roads across Denton were flooded. A trained spotter reported that South Carroll Avenue, one half mile south of US 380, was impassable due to flooding with stalled vehicles.

A Facebook video showed several cars that were stalled in flood waters along US 75 at 15th Street.
An amateur radio operator reported a water rescue occurred near 6600 State Hwy 78 in Sachse.

City of Dallas FRWS indicated that several roads were flooded and closed across northern Dallas, including Park Central Drive at LBJ, Goforth Road at Lanshire Road, West Lawther Drive at NW Highway, and Tantor Road and Luna Road.
Fire Department reported that two vehicles were submerged in high water near 12900 Park Central Drive at the LBJ bridge. One person was killed.
